<!-- thm-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:main}
Let $n \geqslant 2$ and $(T_1, X_1)$,~$(T_{2}, X_2)$, \dots,~$(T_{n}, X_n)$ be transformation monoids each of which is either a full transformation monoid or a symmetric group on a finite non-singleton set.  
Set $\Omega_1=X_1$ and $V_1=T_1$. 
For $2\leqslant i\leqslant n$, let $\Omega_{i}=X_i\times \Omega_{i-1}$ and let $V_i =  T_{i} \operatorname{wr} V_{i-1}$ be the iterated wreath product of $T_i$ by the transformation monoid $(V_{i-1}, \Omega_{i-1})$. Set $V=V_n$. Then
  \[
  \operatorname{rank}(V)=n+t,
  \]
  where $t$ is the number of full transformation monoids among $T_1,\dots, T_n$.
<!-- end thm-1 -->
<!-- lem-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:unitsemiwr}
Let $(S, Y), (R, X)$ be transformation monoids. Suppose that $H\leqslant S$ is the group of units in $S$ and $G\leqslant R$ is the group of units in $R$. Then $S\operatorname{wr} R$ is a monoid and $H\operatorname{wr} G$ is the group of units in $S\operatorname{wr} R$.
<!-- end lem-1 -->
<!-- lem-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:ranksemi}
Let $S$ be a finite semigroup and let $G$ be the group of
units in $S$. If $U\subseteq S$ such that $\langle U\rangle= S$, then $\langle U\cap G\rangle = G$. In particular, 
\[
\operatorname{rank} (S) =\operatorname{rank}(S : G)+\operatorname{rank}(G).
\]
<!-- end lem-2 -->
<!-- lem-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:wrrelarank}
Let $(S, Y), (R, X)$ be transformation monoids. Let $G$ be the group of units of $R$ and let $H$ be the group of units of $S$. If $G$ is transitive on $X$, then
\[
\operatorname{rank}(S\operatorname{wr} R: H\operatorname{wr} G)\leqslant \operatorname{rank}(R:G)+\operatorname{rank}(S:H).
\]
<!-- end lem-3 -->
<!-- prf-1: body_md -->
Lemma~\ref{lem:unitsemiwr} tells us that $H\operatorname{wr} G$ is the group of units of $S\operatorname{wr} R$. Using Lemma~\ref{lem:ranksemi}, in order to prove the lemma, it suffices to verify that 
\[
\operatorname{rank}(S\operatorname{wr} R)\leqslant \operatorname{rank}(H\operatorname{wr} G)+\operatorname{rank}(R:G)+\operatorname{rank}(S:H).
\]
Set $b=\operatorname{rank}(R:G)$ and $c=\operatorname{rank}(S:H)$. Then there exist $r_1,\dots, r_b\in R$ and $s_1, \dots, s_c\in S$ such that $R=\langle G, r_1,\dots, r_b\rangle$ and $S=\langle H, s_1,\dots,s_c \rangle$. We will show that $H\operatorname{wr} G$ along with $(b+c)$ elements generates $S\operatorname{wr} R$. 

Let $\bar e$ be the identity in $S^X$. Then for $1\leqslant i\leqslant b$, let $t_i=(\bar e, r_i)\in S\operatorname{wr} R$. It follows that for any $r\in R$, $(\bar e, r)$ is contained in $T=\langle H\operatorname{wr} G, t_1,\dots, t_b \rangle$. On the other hand, let $x$ be a fixed element of $X$. For each $1\leqslant i\leqslant c$, set
\[
\bar s_i=(e,\dots,e,\underset{\mathclap{\substack{\uparrow \\ \text{$x$\nobreakdash- coordinate}}}}{s_i},e,\dots,e)\in S^X
\]
and set $u_i=(\bar s_i, e)\in S\operatorname{wr} R$. Then for any $s\in S$, the element
\[
((e,\dots,e,\underset{\mathclap{\substack{\uparrow \\ \text{$x$\nobreakdash- coordinate}}}}{s},e,\dots,e), e)
\]
is contained in $U=\langle T, u_1,\dots, u_c\rangle$. As $G$ is a transitive on $X$ and $G$ is contained in $U$, the direct product $S^X$ is contained in $U$ as well. We then deduce that $S\operatorname{wr} R=\langle H\operatorname{wr} G, t_1,\dots, t_b, u_1,\dots, u_c\rangle$, and so the lemma holds.
<!-- end prf-1 -->
<!-- cor-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:unititwr}
Let $V,W$ be defined above. Then $W$ is the group of units in $V$.
<!-- end cor-1 -->
<!-- lem-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:semiup}
Let $V,W$ be defined as before. Then
\[
\operatorname{rank}(V:W)\leqslant \sum_{i=1}^n \operatorname{rank}(T_i:G_i).
\]
<!-- end lem-4 -->
<!-- prf-2: body_md -->
The lemma can be proved by induction on $n$. Lemma~\ref{lem:wrrelarank}  establishes the case when $n=2$.
Now let $n>2$ and suppose that the lemma holds for iterated wreath products of transformation monoids involving fewer than $n$ factors. 
Note that we can treat the iterated wreath products $V$ and $W$ as $V=T_n\operatorname{wr} V_{n-1}$ and $W=G_n\operatorname{wr} W_{n-1}$. 
Combining the inductive hypothesis, corollary~\ref{cor:unititwr} and Lemma~\ref{lem:wrrelarank} yields that
\[
\operatorname{rank}(V:W)\leqslant \operatorname{rank}(T_n:G_n)+\operatorname{rank}(V_{n-1}:W_{n-1})\leqslant \sum_{i=1}^n \operatorname{rank}(T_i:G_i)
\]
as required.
<!-- end prf-2 -->
<!-- lem-5: body_md -->
\label{lem:semihomo}
Let $1\leqslant i\leqslant n-1$. For $\eta_i$ and $\theta_i$ as defined above,
\[
(xv)\eta_i=(x\eta_i)(v\theta_i)
\]
for all $x\in\Omega$ and $v\in V$.
<!-- end lem-5 -->
<!-- prf-3: body_md -->
For $1\leqslant i\leqslant n-1$, let $\pi_i:V_{i+1}\to V_i$ be the natural projection
 semigroup homomorphism, and let $\varphi_i:\Omega_{i+1}\to\Omega_{i}$ 
 be the natural projection. 
 Observe that $\theta_i=\pi_{n-1}\pi_{n-2}\dots\pi_{i}$ and 
 $\eta_i=\varphi_{n-1}\varphi_{n-2}\dots\varphi_{i}$. 
 For $x\in\Omega_{i+1}$ and $v\in V_{i+1}$, 
 by Equation~\eqref{eq:semigroupaction}, $(x v)\varphi_i=(x\varphi_i)(v\pi_i)$.  
 By using this equation repeatedly, we have
 \begin{align*}
 (xv)\eta_i&=(xv)\varphi_{n-1}\varphi_{n-2}\dots\varphi_{i}\\
 &=((x\varphi_{n-1})(v\pi_{n-1}))\varphi_{n-2}\varphi_{n-3}\dots\varphi_{i}\\
 &=((x\varphi_{n-1}\varphi_{n-1})(v\pi_{n-1}\pi_{n-2}))\varphi_{n-3}\varphi_{n-4}\dots\varphi_{i}\\
 &=\dots\\
 &=(x\eta_i)(v\theta_i)
 \end{align*}
 as required.
<!-- end prf-3 -->
<!-- lem-6: body_md -->
\label{lem:kercap}
Let $g\in W$ be a unit in $V$. 
Let $1\leqslant i, j\leqslant n$ with $i\neq j$ such that $\operatorname{rank}(T_i:G_i)=\operatorname{rank}(T_j:G_j)=1$. 
If $x,y\in \Omega$ such that $(x,y)\in \ker(\bar\alpha_i)$ and $(xg, yg)\in\ker(\bar\alpha_j)$, then $x=y$.
<!-- end lem-6 -->
<!-- prf-4: body_md -->
Without loss of generality, we assume that $1\leqslant i<j\leqslant n$, 
since if $j<i$, then we can set $u=xg$ and $v=yg$, and so $x=ug^{-1}, y=vg^{-1}$. Let $x=(x_n, x_{n-1},\dots, x_1)$ and $y=(y_n, y_{n-1},\dots, y_1)$. 
As $(x,y)\in\ker(\bar\alpha_i)$, Equation~\eqref{eq:chap61} gives $x_k=y_k$ except when $k=i$. 
Using Equation~\eqref{eq:chap61}, the fact that $(xg, yg)\in \ker(\bar\alpha_j)$ yields $(xg)\eta_{j-1}=(yg)\eta_{j-1}$.
Because $g$ is a unit, apply Lemma~\ref{lem:semihomo} to observe that $x\eta_{j-1}=y\eta_{j-1}$. Hence $x_i=y_i$, and the lemma holds.
<!-- end prf-4 -->
<!-- lem-7: body_md -->
\label{lem:semilow}
Let $V$ and $W$ be defined as before in this section. Then
\[
\operatorname{rank}(V:W)\geqslant \sum_{i=1}^n \operatorname{rank}(T_i:G_i).
\]
<!-- end lem-7 -->
<!-- prf-5: body_md -->
Set $m=\sum_{i=1}^n \operatorname{rank}(T_i:G_i)$. Suppose that $m=1$. Then $W$ is a proper subsemigroup of $V$, and it follows immediately that $\operatorname{rank}(V:W)\geqslant1$. 

Suppose that $m\geqslant2$. We will prove the lemma by contradiction and we assume that $\operatorname{rank}(V:W)< m$. 
Then there exist $\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_{m-1}\in V\backslash W$ 
such that $V=\langle W, \lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_{m-1}\rangle$. 
Then let $L=\{\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_{m-1}\}$. 
For each $1\leqslant i\leqslant n$ such that $\operatorname{rank}(T_i:G_i)=1$, $\bar\alpha_i$ is a product of the generating set $W\cup L$. 
Note that each $\bar\alpha_i$ is not a unit. 
Then the product for $\bar\alpha_i$ must involve at least one factor from $L$. Thus, for each $\bar\alpha_i$, there exist $g_i\in W$, $v_i\in V$ and an element $\mu_i\in L$, such that $g_i\mu_iv_i=\bar\alpha_i$.
There then exist $i\neq j$ and $\lambda\in L$ such that
$ g_i\lambda v_i=\bar\alpha_i$ and $g_j\lambda v_j=\bar\alpha_j$. It follows that $\lambda v_i=g_{i}^{-1}\bar\alpha_i$ and $\lambda v_j=g_{j}^{-1}\bar\alpha_j$, and so
\[
\ker(\lambda)\subseteq\ker(g_{i}^{-1}\bar\alpha_i)\cap\ker(g_{j}^{-1}\bar\alpha_j).
\]
Since $\lambda$ is not a unit, there exist different elements $a, b\in \Omega$ such that $(a, b)\in\ker(\lambda)$. 
Let $x=ag_i^{-1}$ and $y=bg_i^{-1}$. 
We have $(x, y)\in\ker(\bar\alpha_i)$, $(xg_ig_j^{-1}, yg_ig_j^{-1})\in\ker(\bar\alpha_j)$ and $x\neq y$. However, Lemma~\ref{lem:kercap} tells us that this is impossible. We deduce that $\operatorname{rank}(V:W)\geqslant \sum_{i=1}^n \operatorname{rank}(T_i:G_i)$.
<!-- end prf-5 -->
<!-- lem-8: body_md -->
\label{lem:combine}
For the iterated wreath products of semigroups $V$ and $W$ as defined above,
\[
\operatorname{rank}(V:W)=\sum_{i=1}^n \operatorname{rank}(T_i:G_i).
\]
<!-- end lem-8 -->
